summary: Republican Sen. Steve Daines did not run, so the seat was open. Kurt Alme (Republican) won, ahead of Seth Bodnar (independent) and Alani Bankhead (Democrat).

candidates.name: Kurt Alme
candidates.bio: Kurt Alme is a Republican and former U.S. Attorney for Montana who also served as Gov. Gianforte's budget director. He entered the race in March 2026 after Sen. Steve Daines withdrew and endorsed him.

positions.summary: Says he supports balanced budgets and tax relief, and that deficit spending raises prices.
Says he wants to use Rural Health Transformation Program funds to recruit and retain providers, expand telehealth, and increase price transparency, and opposes subsidizing health insurance companies.
Says "We need to keep the border secure" and calls for investigating drug trafficking organizations "all the way up to the cartels."
Says he supports the Ratepayer Protection Act and wants data center and AI companies to disclose costs and community impacts and protect water quality.

candidates.name: Seth Bodnar
candidates.bio: Seth Bodnar is an independent, a former Army Green Beret and the former president of the University of Montana. He announced his Senate run in March 2026.

positions.summary: Says "tariffs should be used as tools, not toys," wants to cut red tape to build more homes, and wants rules to prevent big private equity firms from buying up large numbers of single-family homes.
Says the recent budget bill "will kick more than 30,000 Montanans off their healthcare," and pledges to defend Medicaid expansion and oppose cuts to critical access hospitals.
Says "we need strong borders and we need to enforce our immigration laws," calls for comprehensive immigration reform, and objects to enforcement he says tramples citizens' individual liberties.
Says communities should have a say before large companies build data centers, wants guardrails in place right away, and supports the Ratepayer Protection Act.
Says "The government has no place in a Montanan's doctor's office, whether that government sits in Helena or Washington, D.C."

candidates.name: Alani Bankhead
candidates.bio: Alani Bankhead is a Democrat who describes herself as a moderate and an independent Democrat. She was the 2026 Democratic nominee for Montana's Senate seat.

positions.summary: Proposes raising the capital gains limit from $250,000 to $500,000 and tax breaks for builders whose projects include at least 30% affordable housing.

Says she would first restore expired ACA tax credits, add a public option and close the coverage gap, then move step by step through "Medicaid for all, then Medicare for all, until everyone is covered."
Says she supports comprehensive immigration reform and wants to streamline the citizenship process.
Says Montana teachers are some of the most poorly paid in the country and that she will fund education because it is the best avenue out of poverty.
Says she opposes AI data center construction in Montana and supports a moratorium.
Lists reproductive freedom among her priorities and says people, not the government, should be trusted.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35). Shares refreshed Nov. 25, 2026 from The Green Papers. State certification was not confirmed.
